Title: A Horrible Combo for the Monocle!

Messages.Author: Halcyan 2
Messages.Body:
With all the recent discussion about the Monocle of Clarity, I just had a
really wild thought -- Monocle of Clarity + Madness of the Bard!

Yeah, both of them are now banned, but wouldn't it be really weird to play with
both of them? And I guess there was indeed a time when you could play with both
of them.

While it wouldn't be too hard for the owner to come up with a rhyming question,
how about the person who needs to answer? Monocle says you can only answer
'yes' or 'no'. So does that mean that he/she loses a pool to Madness of the
Bard every turn?

Halcyan 2

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
halc...@aol.com (Halcyan 2) wrote:
> While it wouldn't be too hard for the owner to come up with a
> rhyming question, how about the person who needs to answer? Monocle
> says you can only answer 'yes' or 'no'. So does that mean that he/she
> loses a pool to Madness of the Bard every turn?

That depends on what your group considers a "rhyme".

He/she could simply make her next statement rhyme with the answer:
"Yes. I confess."
"No. I'm sure it's not so."

--
LSJ (vte...@white-wolf.com) VTES Net.Rep for White Wolf, Inc.

Messages.Author: Andrew Davidson
Messages.Body:
Tom Kassel <tka...@my-deja.com> wrote:

> I saw the Bard for the first time in my playgroup last night (Andrew's
> Bard but the deck was played by another). Next time I will certainly
> dispense with minion D actions to remove it (what a pain the combat
> steps become) and go straight to a poke in the Methuselah's eye.

The card worked better than I expected but it would take a bit more
practise for players to become comfortable with it. As it was, I
didn't notice you losing any blood to the card while the rest of us
lost at least one. The main practical problem seems to be what to make
of a muttered sub-vocalisation. The honour system seems best - where
players volunteer their blood when they fail to rhyme in their own eyes.

Daniel didn't make it easy for you by keeping all his minions
untapped. I'm not sure if this was a deliberate defense of the card or
whether he didn't want to take any initiative himself while still
adjusting to the card's effect.

Anyway, I trust that all these threats of violence are just in jest.
If you really want to spoil the fun then just carry a Sudden Reversal
instead of a big stick. This would be useful to deal with other nasty
master cards like the Vulnerability that I burnt Volker with. Madness
of the Bard was pussy-footing by comparison.

Andrew

Messages.Body:

> required a deal between Dave and myself whereby I rushed some of
> Daniel's minions in return for some good behaviour. The Bard made the

Thats exactly the point! Madness is a great card, I used to have it in my
decks all the time back when I actually could find people to play with. The
whole point of the card is to make it more difficult to create complicated
deals. And yes, that does hinder one style of playing the game, but it does
not hinder all styles of the game. And it no more "subverts important game
features" than cards that make it harder for you to bleed, fight, do
political actions, etc etc etc. Making deals is one way to play the game,
and not the only way, and making it harder for your opponent to play the
want is definately an "important game feature."

Vanda

> I wouldn't bet on it. My defence in court would be justifiable
> homicide. I think I may have an old Louisville Slugger in a cupboard
> at home to keep my hands clean.

The Madness of the Bard is a really bad, bad card and should never,
under any circumstance, be played without a violent response. Same with
that damn Kindred Restructure that changes where everyone sits.

> I deeply loathe the Bard because it subverts important game features
> which are interesting rather than merely silly.

One of the most important aspects of the game is the social
interactions. It is among the things that distinguishes VTES and other
multi-player games from M:tCH wherein most games are only two player.
Madness of the Bard interferes with that. In any case, because we play
all local games by standard tournament rules, MotB is banned from play
in all games in Michigan.

Kindred Restructure is another "punch in the head" card because it's a
pain in the ass to pick up all your stuff and move to another seat.
People that play decks that do that multiple times find themselves on a
little social outing with Joey and Guido.

Regards,
Noal

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
thomas...@ntlworld.com (Tom Kassel) writes:

> My hand was jammed up with Rushes and Ambushes. I had one additional
> strike I could have used but missed - I blame it on going through the
> combat steps in mime. Probably an IG too - unplayed (obviously only
> needed for card flow) due to the Bard induced clumsiness.

In other matters, how many rush cards are you packing?

Common wisdom is 12 rushes (normally Bum's Rush) and 4 Havens in a 90
card tournament style deck. Having more than that generally ups
hand-jam problems. Not that there aren't scenarios where more are
useful, of course, but in a "standard" mono-rush deck, it's a useful
figure to work with. It's also a useful yard-stick even when *not*
playing such a deck e.g. if you diversify your options.
